title: Intertwined complex orbital order and ferrimagnetism in honeycomb molybdate Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$
abstract: Motivated by the recent experimental interest in honeycomb molybdates A$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$, we return and develop the minimal models to capture the essential physics for Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$. It is pointed out that, the magnetism in these materials arises from the mutual induction between the spin-orbit coupling of the tetrahedral sublattice with active orbitals and the superexchange with the spins from the octahedral sublattice. Essentially, the superexchange between the tetrahedral and octahedral sublattices directly drives the ferrimagnetism, and the residual spin-orbit coupling on the tetrahedral sublattice induces the complex orbital order. The hybrid magnon-phonon excitations are further explored together with their resulting Berry curvatures and thermal Hall effect. We discuss the experimental relevance with Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$, and the framework can be extended to FeNiMo$_3$O$_8$, Ni$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$ and other isostructural magnets.
summary: This theoretical work models the magnetic and orbital physics of $	ext{Fe}_2	ext{Mo}_3	ext{O}_8$ by coupling spin, orbital, and lattice degrees of freedom. It predicts a ferrimagnetic ground state characterized by complex orbital order and predicts measurable signatures like a thermal Hall effect via magnon-phonon coupling.
main_problem: The paper investigates the complex interplay between orbital order and ferrimagnetism in the honeycomb molybdate $	ext{Fe}_2	ext{Mo}_3	ext{O}_8$. It seeks to understand how spin-orbit coupling and superexchange drive the magnetic and orbital ground states.
main_result: The system exhibits an anticollinear ferrimagnetic ground state coupled with a complex orbital order on the tetrahedral sites. This coupling leads to hybrid magnon-phonon excitations with nontrivial band topology and a finite thermal Hall effect.
method: The authors developed a minimal Hamiltonian incorporating spin, orbital, and lattice degrees of freedom. They used Holstein-Primakoff expansions and diagonalized the resulting coupled bosonic Hamiltonian in momentum space.
model_or_system: The system is $	ext{Fe}_2	ext{Mo}_3	ext{O}_8$, modeled by $H_{	ext{min}} = H_t + H_o + H_{	ext{ex}}$, which is extended to include phonon ($H_p$) and coupling ($H_D$) terms. The model captures the distinct electronic structures of the tetrahedral and octahedral sublattices.
key_observables: Anticollinear ferrimagnetic order, complex orbital order ($\langle	au_iangle$), magnon-phonon excitation gaps, Berry curvature ($\Omega_n(\mathbf{k})$), and thermal Hall conductivity ($\kappa_{xy}$).
important_parameters: Exchange couplings ($J$), spin-orbit coupling ($\lambda$), and crystal field anisotropy ($D$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on deriving the effective Hamiltonian by treating the system in the ordered orbital sector and using quadratic approximations for the coupled bosonic excitations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the $3d$ crystal field splitting, the schematic of the honeycomb structure, the resulting six magnon-phonon branches with anticrossings, and the calculated Berry curvature and Chern numbers.
paper_structure: The paper systematically builds the Hamiltonian by defining the spin/orbital terms ($H_t, H_o, H_{	ext{ex}}$), then coupling in lattice dynamics ($H_p$) and deriving the full magnon-phonon coupling ($H_D$). Finally, it diagonalizes the coupled system to calculate topological invariants and transport properties.
why_interesting: The explicit inclusion of lattice dynamics (phonons) coupled to electronic excitations (magnons) to generate topological features like the Berry curvature is highly relevant to modern condensed matter theory, bridging magnetism, orbital physics, and topological materials.

Schematic representation of the single-electron 3d crystal field splitting for Fe2+ (3d6) ions at the tetrahedral and octahedral sites in Fe2Mo3O8 under a unified z ∥c-axis frame. At the tetrahedral site, one hole appears in the doubly- degenerate e1 state, leading to an orbital pseudospin τ = 1/2. Conversely, at the trigonal-elongated octahedral site, the local orbitals are quenched.
